sentences.text: Ozarcus was an extinct genus of symmoriiform cartilaginous fish that lived during the Carboniferous period in Arkansas.
This creature possesses branchial arches that show unexpected similarities to bony fish rather than typical cartilaginous fish.
Unlike modern sharks, the first four branchial arches of Ozarcus have two pairs of pharyngobranchials that form a solid roof over the gill cavity, a condition similar to bony fish.
The genus name Ozarcus honors the Ozark Mountains where it was found, and the species name mapesae honors its discoverer G. K. Mapes.
The holotype fossil, a warped but three-dimensionally preserved skull with gill baskets discovered by G. K. Mapes, is cataloged as AMNH FF20544.
A partial braincase previously identified as Cobelodus and described in 2007 was reclassified as Ozarcus in 2017.
Ozarcus was initially tentatively classified within the family Falcatidae due to its small teeth resembling those of Falcatus and Damocles.
Later research repositioned Ozarcus as a sister taxon to Dwykaselachus or near the base of Symmoriiformes, separating it from the falcatid Damocles.
Ozarcus lived during the Serpukhovian stage, approximately 330.3 to 326.9 million years ago.
